system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook**

The Seller's note says [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny. Nothing in our file shows that Wattlebridge has agreed them, so I have reviewed all 16 items against the playbook.

| ID | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** General liability cap | 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl. 12.1) | 25%, AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a fallback only. | **Reject; counter at 25%.** No written authority from Amelia Frost exists, so 20% cannot be offered. |
| **SPA-N-002** De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, recoverable only above the basket (excess-only) (cl. 12.2) | De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery once exceeded | **Reject.** The Seller's figures are five times our thresholds and make the basket a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003** General claims time limit | 18 months after Completion. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise (cl. 12.3/13) | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval. No limitation should sweep across categories. | **Reject.** The "applies to all Claims" wording is a hidden override of the separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004** Fundamental / Title regime | Capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject.** Title is not an administrative simplification; it is a core protection. |
| **SPA-N-005** Fraud carve-out | No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **Reject; insert carve-out.** The current drafting would bar fraud claims. |
| **SPA-N-006** Disclosure scope | Whole data room (DL 1.1, including DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2) | Specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2.** Deemed disclosure of the whole data room would waive most of our claims. |
| **SPA-N-007** Buyer knowledge | No claim for anything Buyer or advisers knew or could discover from data room or public records (cl. 8.3) | Delete blanket exclusions. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject.** A discoverability test would bar claims on the very issues DD-002 to DD-012 raise. |
| **SPA-N-008** Bluefen consent | Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's consent (cl. 3/6.3). DL: no final consent or evidence of conditions. | Effective consent and evidence that conditions 11.2/11.3 are satisfied before Completion, as a condition precedent | **Reject.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), so reasonable endeavours is insufficient and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. |
| **SPA-N-009** Riverlark facility | Release provided after Completion (cl. 2/7). DL: about AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. | **Reject.** Paying out at Completion is the only clean route; a post-Completion release leaves us exposed to the lender's security. |
| **SPA-N-010** Employee bonuses | AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow as "a matter for the Seller". On-costs not addressed (DL 5). | Specific funds-flow line item or Seller funding, including triggered on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) | **Reject.** The funds flow must not silently drop a known liability. Require a line item and quantified on-costs. |
| **SPA-N-011** Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as adequate (cl. 11.1). DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, not independently verified. DL 4: no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Broaden the narrow indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure route. Do not rely on the AUD 180,000 figure either way. | **Reject narrowing; broaden.** Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on payment, and the file does not show payment was made. |
| **SPA-N-012** Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | "Preliminary, not expected to be material" (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6). DL 6: possible export of about 1,240 records; access and notification unknown. | Preserve logs, investigate, require regular updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Do not accept "not material".** The facts are unresolved, so require preservation, investigation and updates rather than a characterisation. |
| **SPA-N-013** Sandbar renewals | Ordinary-course operating costs; AUD 330,000 aggregate (DL 8: not stated whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued) | Assess the renewals. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Assess before accepting.** Request terms and timing, but do not reclassify as Debt or deduct from price on current information. |
| **SPA-N-014** Category separation | All matters folded into the general regime for "administrative simplicity" | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **Reject.** Combining categories undermines the separate protections in SPA-N-004 and SPA-N-016. |
| **SPA-N-015** Title verification | Title evidenced by Company share register (DD-012); DL 10 notes no Buyer verification | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. | **Reject reliance on DD-012.** An internal register is not independent evidence of title. |
| **SPA-N-016** Tax / IP open terms | Tax and IP warranty positions "settled" under the general regime | Treat as OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | **Reject as settled.** Keep open for separate negotiation; do not accept the general regime as resolving these. |

**Items needing Amelia Frost's written approval before any movement:**
- 20% cap (SPA-N-001), which also needs the draft identified in writing
- 18-month claims period (SPA-N-003)
- Any post-Completion Riverlark release (SPA-N-009)

None has been given, so none of these fallbacks should be offered in the mark-up.
=== END ADVICE ===
